title: Lane
description: molds/<mold_id>/testing/<lane>/lane.json — what .claude/scripts/lanes.py runs for this lane. The lane declares itself; adding a lane to a future mold never edits the runner.

lane.description: Must be one of the five the application schema can record. Anything else is a runner error, not a silent skip: the result would have nowhere legal to live.

order.description: Run order across lanes; ties broken by name. functional 10, context 20, load 30, accessibility 40, responsiveness 50.

summary.description: One line, printed in the report header.

not_covered.description: What this lane does NOT check, printed verbatim in the report so a green lane cannot imply more than it measured.

requires.description: Lane-level: any unmet precondition skips the WHOLE lane, quoting its `else`.

checks.description: Empty or absent means the lane has no harness: `skipped`, never `pass`.

name.description: Unique within the lane; becomes the report row.

cwd.description: Default codebase. `codebase` is what THIS application ships: build/<app_id>.lane/ (mold + packs, the app's own deployment profile) for an app with packs, else molds/<mold_id>/codebase. `default_profile` is where the mold's OWN offline tests run: build/<app_id>.lane-default/ (mold + the packs' code, the DEFAULT profile) for an app with packs, else molds/<mold_id>/codebase. The mold's tests pin the default profile's words and fields, so on a relabelling pack's profile they fail by design (mold_v1-146/147); grade the app's own words with a `codebase` check.

timeout_s.description: Default 600. A timeout is a FAIL with reason 'timed out after Ns'.

stdout.description: Every regex must match combined stdout+stderr.

stdout_not.description: None may match. This is how a lane refuses to grade on a status code.

skip_on.description: Judged after exit/stdout/stdout_not, so a failure is never hidden: if `stdout` matches, the check ran but declared part of what it names unmeasured, and is recorded `skipped` (never `pass`) with `else` as the reason; its measured rows still print. The lane is then `skipped`, never `pass`.

else.description: What the operator should do, in one sentence with the command in it; placeholders allowed.

requires.description: Check-level: unmet means this check is SKIPPED, never failed — and a lane with a skipped check can never be `pass`.

emits.description: stdout is a markdown table, inlined verbatim under 'Measured rows'.

known_defect.description: A task id. ANNOTATION ONLY: it never changes the verdict. It links the task in the report and stops a duplicate task being filed.

why.description: One sentence: what a failure here actually means.

app_env.description: Names of THIS application's own secrets to place in the check's environment, read at run time from where the app's state says they live (the Vercel project's env for secret_store vercel_env, infra/vm/apps/<app>/.env for vm_env_file). Values are never printed, logged or stored; the report shows names only. A name that cannot be supplied makes the check skipped, never failed. Exists so a check that must connect AS the application (test:org-isolation, which is meaningless as a BYPASSRLS role) can run against a deployed app without anyone copying a URL into a file.

precondition.description: Exactly one of state/env/path/cmd, plus `else`: one imperative sentence naming a runnable command.

must.description: 'nonempty', or a literal the value must equal.

must_not.description: A literal the value must not equal.

env.description: Environment variable presence BY NAME. The value is never read, logged or stored.

path.description: Path relative to the repo root; placeholders allowed.

else.description: What the operator should do, in one sentence with the command in it.
